workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§136–139
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§136–139: The Jurkin Punished, and Högelün's Four Foster-Sons
part: §§136–139 — The Jurkin Punished, and Högelün's Four Foster-Sons
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§136–139, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Four sections. §136 tells of the Jurkin's stripping and killing of men left behind in the rear camps, Chinggis's speech against them (the Tatar campaign they failed to join), his ride against them at Dolqan-Boldaq, and the seizing of Sacha-Beki and Taichu, who put themselves aside by their own words. §137 has the Jurkin people set in motion; of the three sons of Telegetü-Bayan of the Jalair among them, Kügün-Uqa and Chila'un-Gaichi each bring two sons to Chinggis and give them into service under oaths with the penalties named, Jebke is given to Qasar, and a boy, Boroqul, is brought to Mother Högelün. §138 lists the four boys she took in and raised: Küchü, Kököchü, Shigigen-Qutuqu and Boroqul. §139 explains the name Jurkin as 'those no one can withstand' and tells how Chinggis broke them and made their people his own. Several words, in the oaths especially, rest on the Ming glosses alone, and the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u aγ̇uruγ Hariltu naγ̇ur-a büleġei.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
genitive: of … (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [的]
rear camp, the camp of the old and the young (Ming 老小營; 'rear camp' is my rendering) [老小營]
past: 'there was, used to be' (a variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan's rear-camp, Hariltu lake-at, there was.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan's rear camp was at Lake Hariltu.
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u aγ̇uruγ is 'Chinggis Qahan's rear camp' (Ming 老小營, 'the camp of the old and the young'; 'rear camp' is my rendering); Hariltu is only 'water name' in the Ming, and naγ̇ur-a (海子行) puts it at a lake with the dative-locative -a. büleġei is 'there was, used to be'. The possessor stands before its noun: Qaγan-(n)u aγ̇uruγ.

sentences.t: Aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur qosoruγsan-i Žürkin tabin haran-u qubčan tonožuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 阿兀舌魯兀惕-圖舌兒 Aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur

morph.gloss: rear camp (Ming 老小營) [老小營]
plural (the printed aγ̇uruγ̇ud has -ud after γ) [(每)]

words.reading: 中豁搠舌魯黑撒泥 qosoruγsan-i

morph.gloss: to be left behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種名]
to strip, plunder (stem inferred from the Ming 剝脫) [剝脫了]

sentences.l: Rear-camps-in left-behind-ones-(acc.) Žürkin fifty people's clothing stripped.
sentences.i: The Jurkin stripped the clothing of fifty men who had been left behind in the rear camps.
sentences.n: Aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur is the plural 'rear camps' with the dative-locative -tur (Ming 裏); qosoruγsan-i is a participle, 'the ones left behind' (落後的), with the accusative -i. I read it as the object, with haran-u qubčan 'fifty people's clothing' saying what was taken; the Ming leaves the grammar loose, so this is a reading. tonožuγ̇ui (剝脫了) 'stripped' ends in a past -žuγ̇ui; the stem is read from the Ming. Shiratori's stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Harban haran-i alažuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Ten people-(acc.) killed.
sentences.i: And ten men they killed.
sentences.n: Harban haran-i alažuγ̇ui: 'ten men (accusative) killed' (Ming 十 人行 殺了). The subject, the Jurkin, is not repeated; alažuγ̇ui has the same past ending as tonožuγ̇ui before it.

sentences.t: Žürukin-e tein kigdebe: keġen

morph.gloss: the Jurkin (a spelling of Žürkin) [種(名)]
dative-locative: to, by (front-vowel form); with a passive verb it can name the doer [行]

sentences.l: Žürukin-by thus was-done: saying
sentences.i: "This was done by the Jurkin," they said,
sentences.n: kigdebe (被做了) is ki- 'do' with the passive -gde-, 'was done'. The Jurkin stand in the dative, Žürukin-e (Ming 行); with a passive the dative names the doer, so 'was done by the Jurkin' (a spelling of Žürkin with an extra u). keġen is the converb 'saying', closing the report. Who speaks is told in the next unit.

sentences.t: bidan-u aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur qosoruγsad Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a žaγ̇abasu

morph.gloss: stem-final n before a case ending

words.reading: 阿兀舌魯兀惕-圖舌兒 aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur

morph.gloss: rear camp (Ming 老小營) [老小營]
plural (the printed aγ̇uruγ̇ud has -ud after γ) [(每)]

words.reading: 中豁搠舌魯黑撒惕 qosoruγsad

morph.gloss: to be left behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後]
past participle, plural: 'those who have …ed' [的每]
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [行]
to tell, report (stem inferred from the Ming 吿) [吿呵]

sentences.l: Us-of rear-camps-in left-behind-ones Čiṅgis Qaγan-to when-told,
sentences.i: and when those left behind in our rear camps told this to Chinggis Qahan,
sentences.n: bidan-u is 'our' (bida with a stem-n and the genitive -u), put before aγ̇uruγ̇ud-tur 'in the rear camps'. qosoruγsad is the plural participle 'those left behind' (Ming 落後的每). Qaγan-(n)a (皇帝行) is the dative 'to the Qahan'. žaγ̇abasu (吿呵) is 'when told'; the stem is read from the Ming and the ending is the Ming's 呵 'if, when'.

sentences.t: ene kelen sonosuγ̇ad Čiṅgis Qaγan maši kiliṅlažu

morph.gloss: converb of completed action: having …ed (back-vowel form)
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]

sentences.l: This word having-heard, Čiṅgis Qaγan greatly angering,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, hearing this word, was greatly angered
sentences.n: sonosuγ̇ad is the converb of completed action, 'having heard'. kiliṅlažu (怒着) is 'angering, being angry', a converb in -žu; the stem kiliṅla- is read from the Ming. A short converb chain, broken here at the speech that follows.

sentences.t: ügülerün: "Žürkin-(n)e ker ein kigden büleġei bida.

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種名]
dative: by, to (front-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's); here marks the doer of a passive [(行)]
how, in what manner (interrogative adverb) [怎生]
past: 'there was, used to be' (a variant of -leġe)

sentences.l: saying: Žürkin-by how thus being-done was we.
sentences.i: and said, "How have the Jurkin done this to us?
sentences.n: ügülerün is the time-converb 'when saying'. Žürkin-(n)e is the dative (Ming 行) and, with kigden (被做 'being done', the passive again), the doer: 'by the Jurkin'. ker ein 'how thus', büleġei 'was', bida 'we'. So literally 'how thus being-done was we, by the Jurkin'; I read 'how have the Jurkin done this to us'. Shiratori's quotation mark opens at Žürkin-(n)e and closes only at bolulaγ̇i" in unit 12, so units 6 to 12 are one speech of Chinggis's; that is why bida 'we' returns, and why i opens the quotation here and closes it in unit 12.

sentences.t: Onan-(n)u tün-dür qurimlaqui- dur baγ̇urči Šikiγ̇ur-i müd-kü ašigiba.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [的]
forest, wood (uncertain; stem not otherwise known) [林]
participle ending: …ing (the word is broken by Shiratori's hyphen before dur)
dative-locative: at, in (back-vowel form; Ming 時 'time'), so 'at the time of' [時]
cook, steward of the food [厨子]
Shikiur, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; analysis uncertain) [他每]
particle: also, even (Ming 也; uncertain) [也]
to strike, beat (stem inferred from the Ming 打) [打了]

sentences.l: Onan's forest-in feasting-at cook Šikiγ̇ur-(acc.) they also struck.
sentences.i: In the forest of the Onan, at the time of the feast, they struck the cook Shikiur too,
sentences.n: Onan-(n)u tün-dür is 'in the Onan's forest' (Ming 河名的 林裏); tün 'forest' is not known to me otherwise, so only the Ming 林 is firm. qurimlaqui- dur is one word split by Shiratori's hyphen: qurim 'feast', a verb-maker, a participle, and -dur 'at', Ming 時 'time': 'at the time of feasting'. müd-kü (他每也) is 'they also'; I take müd as 'they' and -kü as 'also' on the Ming alone. ašigiba 'struck' has its stem read from the Ming 打. The unit is inside Chinggis's speech (see unit 6).

sentences.t: Belgütei-jin mürü müd-kü čabčiba.

morph.gloss: Belgütei, a man's name (a younger brother of Chinggis, as the earlier parts give him) [人名]
they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; analysis uncertain) [他每]
particle: also, even (Ming 也; uncertain) [也]
to cut, chop (stem inferred from the Ming 砍) [砍了]

sentences.l: Belgütei's shoulder they also cut.
sentences.i: and cut Belgütei's shoulder too.
sentences.n: Belgütei-jin mürü is 'Belgütei's shoulder' (-jin is the genitive after a vowel); čabčiba (砍了) 'cut'. The same müd-kü 'they also' as before. This is the wound told in §131.

sentences.t: žokilduja keġegdežü Qorižin Qatun, Quγ̇určin žirin-i ičuγ̇ažu ögbe bida.

morph.gloss: to be fitting, agree (stem inferred from the Ming 商和) [商和咱]
Qorijin, a woman's name (personal name) [婦名]
lady, queen, a qan's wife [娘(子)]
Qughurchin, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦)名]
to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred from the Ming 退) [退着]
causative: make …, so 'make withdraw, send back'

sentences.l: 'Let-us-agree' being-said, Qorižin Qatun, Quγ̇určin, the two-(acc.) causing-to-withdraw gave we.
sentences.i: When they said, 'Let us come to terms,' we gave back the two ladies, Qorijin Qatun and Qughurchin.
sentences.n: žokilduja (商和咱) is a hortative: žoki- 'be fitting' (stem read from the Ming) with the reciprocal -ldu- and -ja 'let us'. keġegdežü is 'being told' (the passive of keġe-). ičuγ̇ažu (退着) is ič- 'withdraw' with the causative -uγ̇a-, which I read as 'make withdraw, send back', then ögbe 'gave', bida 'we'. So 'we gave back the two ladies'; the two women are the ones taken in §131. Who proposed the peace is not said; 'they' is my reading. bida 'we' is Chinggis speaking for his side (units 6 to 12).

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina erten-ü öšiten kigten ebüges ečiges-i bidan-u baraγsad Tatar-i qamsan morilaja keġen

morph.gloss: that, he (the stem is teġün- before the genitive) [那]
grudge, feud (stem read from the Ming 讐) [讐]
resentment, grievance (stem inferred from the Ming 怨) [怨]
stem-final n before a case ending
to be finished, ruined; with an accusative, 'to finish off' (uncertain) [了了]
past participle, plural: 'those who have …ed' [的(每)]
to join, combine, act together (stem inferred from the Ming 併) [逼併]
to mount a horse, ride out (mori 'horse' + verb-maker) [上馬咱]

sentences.l: That-of after, former grudge-having resentment-having forefathers fathers-(acc.) ours having-ruined Tatars-(acc.) together let-us-ride, saying:
sentences.i: After that we said, 'Let us ride together against the Tatars, our old foes and enemies, who ruined our forefathers and fathers,'
sentences.n: Teġün-ü qoina is 'after that' (tere has the stem teġün- before the genitive). erten-ü öšiten kigten (在前的 讐有的 怨有的) are 'those of old having grudges, having resentments': -ten is the possessive plural. baraγsad (了了的) is the plural participle 'those who have ruined' (the stem bara- is uncertain); its objects are ebüges ečiges-i, 'forefathers, fathers'. Tatar-i is the accusative object of morilaja, 'let us ride', hortative -ja; qamsan (逼併) 'joining, together'. The Ming 逼併 may mean pressing in a body; I read 'together'. keġen has no subject of its own; inside Chinggis's speech (units 6 to 12), where bida 'we' recurs, I read 'we said'.

sentences.t: Žürkin-i Žirγoγ̇an üdüd külčežü ese-kü iregdebe.

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種(名)]
particle: also, even (Ming 也; uncertain) [也]
to break, be broken; or ire- 'come' with a passive (stem and sense uncertain; Ming 破來了) [破來了]

sentences.l: Žürkin-(acc.) six days waiting not-also came-broke.
sentences.i: We waited six days for the Jurkin, and they did not come.
sentences.n: Žürkin-i Žirγoγ̇an üdüd külčežü: 'waiting for the Jurkin for six days' (üdüd is the plural of üdür, Ming (日)每); the waiters are not named, and in Chinggis's speech I read 'we'. ese-kü iregdebe: ese 'not' and the Ming 不曾也; iregdebe is glossed 破來了, 'broke, came', which does not fit a plain ire- 'come'. The previous part reads iregdeküi as ire- with the passive -gde-, and the grammar here is uncertain; I take the sense as 'they did not come' and i says no more than that.

sentences.t: Edöġe basa daisun-dur šiqan daisun müd-kü bolulaγ̇i" keġeġed Čiṅgis Qaγan Žürkin-dür morilaba.

morph.gloss: to lean on, press close to (stem inferred from the Ming 挨) [挨着]
they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; analysis uncertain) [他每]
particle: also, even (Ming 也; uncertain) [也]
to become, be made (bolu-, as in boluba and boluγ̇ad; Ming 做) [做]
past: 'became, has become' (the back-vowel partner of -leġei in büleġei and keġeldüleġei; Ming 了; uncertain) [了]
converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種(名)]
to mount a horse, ride out [上馬了]

sentences.l: Now again enemy-at pressing, enemy they also became, saying, Čiṅgis Qaγan Žürkin-against rode.
sentences.i: Now, once more leaning on the enemy, they too have become enemies," he said, and Chinggis Qahan rode out against the Jurkin.
sentences.n: Edöġe basa 'now again'; daisun-dur šiqan daisun müd-kü bolulaγ̇i (敵行 挨着 敵 他每也 做了) is, word for word, 'at the enemy leaning, enemy they also became'. bolulaγ̇i is bolu- 'become' with -laγ̇i, the back-vowel partner of -leġei (büleġei, keġeldüleġei): a past. The Ming glosses it 了, as it glosses the other pasts, where the hortatives carry 咱 (morilaja 上馬咱 in unit 10); so 'they too have become enemies', not 'let us make'. 'Leaning on the enemy' I take to mean leaning on the Tatars, whom the speech has just named, but the Mongol says only 'the enemy'; the reading is a guess from the Ming. The quotation closes at bolulaγ̇i"; keġeġed 'having said' closes the speech; morilaba 'rode out' (morila-, from mori 'horse'). Shiratori's stop closes the whole sentence. Twelve words, kept whole.

sentences.t: Žürkin-i Kelüren-ü Ködöġe-Aral-ün Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ̇ud-ta büküi-dür irgen in-ü daγ̇uliba.

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種(名)]
Ködöġe-Aral, a place (Ming 地名 only; aral perhaps 'island', as in Baljun-Aral) [地名]

words.reading: 朶羅安-孛勒荅兀惕-塔 Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ̇ud-ta

morph.gloss: Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ, a place (Ming 地名 only) [地名]
people, subjects (the common folk of a camp or realm) [百姓]
his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]

sentences.l: Žürkin-(acc.) Kelüren's Ködöġe-Aral's Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ̇ud-at being-when, people their plundered.
sentences.i: While the Jurkin were at Dolqan-Boldaq in Ködöge-Aral on the Kerülen, he plundered their people.
sentences.n: A chain of genitives, each before its noun: Kelüren-ü Ködöġe-Aral-ün Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ̇ud-ta, 'of the Kelüren, of Ködöġe-Aral, at Dolγ̇an-Boldaγ̇ud'. The Ming says only 'river name', 'place name', 'place name'. büküi-dür is 'while being, when (they) were' (Ming 有 時). irgen in-ü daγ̇uliba: 'their people he plundered'. Žürkin-i is an accusative before büküi-dür; I read it as 'the Jurkin, while they were…'. Boldaγ̇ud carries a plural -ud; the Ming says only 'place name'.

sentences.t: Sača-Beki, Taiču qojar čüġen bejes(i)-jen dutaγ̇aba.

morph.gloss: Sacha-Beki, a man's name (personal name; the sense of beki is not known from these sources) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
two, the two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [自的行]
to flee, run away (Ming 走) [走了]

sentences.l: Sača-Beki, Taiču, the two, few, with-their-own-bare-bodies fled.
sentences.i: Sacha-Beki and Taichu, the two, with few men, bare of all but themselves, fled.
sentences.n: qojar 'the two' follows the pair, Sača-Beki and Taiču. čüġen (少) is 'few'. bejes(i)-jen is beje 'body' with a plural -s and the reflexive -(i)jen, 'their own bodies'; the Ming 罄身 means 'with nothing but the body', so 'bare of all but themselves'. dutaγ̇aba (走了) 'fled'. Shiratori's stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Qoināča an-u nekežü Teletü amasar-a güjičežü Sača-Beki, Taiču qojar-i bariba.

morph.gloss: their (third-person plural genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to attack, pursue (stem uncertain; Ming 襲) [襲着]
Teletü, a place (Ming 地名 only) [地名]
to overtake, catch up (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
Sacha-Beki, a man's name (personal name; the sense of beki is not known from these sources) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to seize, take hold of [拿了]

sentences.l: From-behind them pursuing, Teletü mouth-at overtaking, Sača-Beki, Taiču, the two-(acc.) took-hold-of.
sentences.i: Pursuing them from behind and overtaking them at the mouth of the Teletü, he seized Sacha-Beki and Taichu, the two.
sentences.n: A converb chain: nekežü 'attacking, pursuing' and güjičežü 'overtaking' (stems read from the Ming 襲, 趕上), ending in bariba 'seized'. Qoināča is 'from behind' (qoina with a short ablative -ča); an-u is 'their' and stands after what it modifies. Teletü is 'place name' in the Ming; amasar-a is 'at the mouth' (Ming 口行). qojar-i is the accusative 'the two'.

sentences.t: Barižu Čiṅgis Qaγan Sača, Taiču qojar-a ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to seize, take hold of [拿着]
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
Sacha, a man's name (short for Sača-Beki; Ming 人名) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Seizing, Čiṅgis Qaγan Sača, Taiču, the two-to saying:
sentences.i: Having seized them, Chinggis Qahan said to the two, Sacha and Taichu:
sentences.n: Barižu 'having seized' (converb -žu, back-vowel) starts a new sentence by Shiratori's capital, taking up bariba of the line before. qojar-a is the dative, 'to the two'. ügülerün 'when saying'; the colon opens the speech.

sentences.t: "Erte üdür bida jaγ̇u keġeldüleġei"

morph.gloss: early, in former times (adjective, adverb) [在先]

sentences.l: Formerly day we what said-together?
sentences.i: "On that earlier day, what did we say to one another?"
sentences.n: Erte üdür 'in former times, day', bida jaγ̇u 'we, what', keġeldüleġei 'said to one another': keġe- 'say' with the reciprocal -ldü- and the past -leġei (Ming 共說來, 'said together'). Shiratori's quotation marks open at Erte and close here.

sentences.t: keġegdežü Sača, Taiču qojar ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Sacha, a man's name (short for Sača-Beki; Ming 人名) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
two, the two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]

sentences.l: Being-told, Sača, Taiču, the two saying:
sentences.i: Being so spoken to, Sacha and Taichu, the two, said:
sentences.n: keġegdežü (被說着) is the passive converb, 'being told', which I read as 'being so addressed'. Then qojar 'the two' and ügülerün 'when saying'; the speech they make comes next.

sentences.t: "Ügülegsen üge-dür(i)-jen ba ese kürbe.

morph.gloss: past participle: 'that has been …ed' (Ming 說了的)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's) [自的行]
we (first-person plural, exclusive; Ming 俺) [俺]

sentences.l: Spoken word-in-own we not arrived.
sentences.i: "We did not hold to the word we spoke."
sentences.n: Ügülegsen is the participle 'that was spoken' (Ming 說了的); üge-dür(i)-jen is 'in one's own word', with the dative-locative -dür and the reflexive -(i)jen. ba 'we' (Ming 俺), ese kürbe 'did not arrive' (kür- 'reach'). I read 'arrive at the word' as 'keep to the word', because the Ming gives only 不曾 到了, 'did not reach'; the idiom is not certain.

sentences.t: Üges-tür man-u kürge" keġeġed

morph.gloss: we (exclusive); man- is its stem before the genitive [俺]
to bring to, deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain; here a bare stem, perhaps an imperative) [敎到]
converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: Words-in ours bring-to, saying
sentences.i: "Let it be brought to pass in our words," they said,
sentences.n: Üges-tür is 'in the words' (plural üges, locative -tür); man-u is 'ours' (the stem man- of ba 'we' with the genitive -u, standing after the word it belongs to), so 'in our words'. kürge (敎到) is the causative of kür- 'reach', 'cause to arrive', here a bare stem, which I read as an imperative: 'let it be brought to pass'. The sense is that of an oath, 'let it be done in our words'; unit 22 looks back on it in the same terms (üġes-tür an-u kürgen, 'in their words … bringing'). The Mongol has no 'to us' (man-u is a genitive), and I cannot say more than the Ming does. keġeġed closes the speech.

sentences.t: üges(i)-jen mederežü tüšižü ögbe.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's) [自的行]
to know (stem inferred from the Ming 敎知) [敎知着]
verbal suffix (uncertain; the Ming has 敎 'cause')
to stretch out (the neck) (stem inferred from the Ming 伸頸) [伸頸着]

sentences.l: Words-own making-known, neck stretching-out, gave.
sentences.i: Having made their words known, they stretched out their necks and gave them.
sentences.n: üges(i)-jen is 'their own words'. mederežü (敎知着) is 'making known' (a causative sense in the Ming 敎; the stem mede- 'know' is read from it). tüšižü (伸頸着) 'stretching the neck'; ögbe 'gave'. What is given is not said; the Ming picture is of offering the neck, and I read 'gave them' for 'gave themselves up'. Shiratori's stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Üges-i an-u medereġülžü üġes-tür an-u kürgen büteġežü mün tende gebe.

morph.gloss: their (third-person plural genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to know (stem inferred from the Ming 敎知) [敎知着]
their (third-person plural genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to bring to, deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain) [送到]
to complete, bring about (Ming 完備; stem uncertain) [完備着]
just, the very, the same (Ming 只) [只]
there, then (locative adverb, from tere 'that') [那裏]
to cast aside, abandon (Ming 撇了; perhaps a short form of gedkü-; uncertain) [撇了]

sentences.l: Words-(acc.) their causing-to-know, words-in their delivering completing, just there cast-aside.
sentences.i: Having had their words made known, and carried out to the letter in their words, he cast them aside there and then.
sentences.n: A converb chain: medereġülžü 'causing to be known' (causative -ġül-), kürgen 'bringing to', büteġežü 'bringing to completion' (Ming 完備着), ending in gebe (撇了) 'cast aside'. an-u is 'their' after its noun. mün tende 'just there'. The Ming does not say what 'cast aside' means here; the oaths of §137 use the same word, and I read it as that they were put aside, that is executed, by their own words. Subject unspoken, presumably Chinggis.

sentences.t: Sača, Taiču qojar-i büteġed qarižu irežü

morph.gloss: Sacha, a man's name (short for Sača-Beki; Ming 人名) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to complete, bring about (Ming 完備; stem uncertain) [完備了]
converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: Sača, Taiču, the two-(acc.) having-finished, returning, coming
sentences.i: Having finished with Sacha and Taichu, the two, he came back,
sentences.n: büteġed (完備了) is the converb of completed action 'having completed'; qarižu irežü 'returning, coming' are two converbs in a chain, 'came back'. 'Finished with' for büteġed is my reading of the Ming 'completed'; it may mean dealt with.

sentences.t: Žürkin-ü irge ködölgeküi-dür Žalair-un Telegetü- Bajan-u köġün Küġün-Uγ̇a, Čilaγ̇un-Γaiči, Žebke γurban tede Žürkin-dür ažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種(名)]
people (Ming 百姓; read as a short form of irgen, since the 'wether' irge of earlier parts does not fit the Ming) [百姓]

words.reading: 歌多勒格恢-突︀舌兒 ködölgeküi-dür

morph.gloss: to move (stem inferred from the Ming 動) [敎動]
Telegetü, a man's name (Ming 人名; joined with the next word, Bajan-u) [人名]
Küġün-Uγ̇a, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Chila'un-Gaichi, a man's name (Ming 人名; the sense of Γaiči is not known from these sources) [人名]
Jebke, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan [種名]

sentences.l: Žürkin's people when-setting-in-motion, Žalair's Telegetü-Bajan's sons Küġün-Uγ̇a, Čilaγ̇un-Γaiči, Žebke, three, those Žürkin-among were.
sentences.i: When he was setting the Jurkin people in motion, there were among the Jurkin those three, Kügün-Uqa, Chila'un-Gaichi and Jebke, sons of Telegetü-Bayan of the Jalair.
sentences.n: ködölgeküi-dür (敎動 時) is 'when making move': ködöl-, the causative -ge-, the participle -küi and the locative -dür. Then a chain of genitives: Žalair-un Telegetü-Bajan-u köġün, 'of the Jalair, of Telegetü-Bajan, son(s)'. The Ming glosses Bajan as 富的 'rich', so Telegetü-Bajan may be 'rich Telegetü'; I keep it as a name. tede 'those' and γurban 'three' follow the three names; ažuγ̇ui 'were' (Ming 有來).

sentences.t: Küġün-Uγ̇a Muqali, Buqa qojar köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen aγ̇ulžažü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Küġün-Uγ̇a, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Muqali, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Buqa, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
two, the two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
instrumental: with (the bracketed (i)s of köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen are Shiratori's; as in the earlier köġüd(i)-jer-en, 'with one's own sons')
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [自的行]
to have an audience, to be received, to wait on a lord (Ming 拜見) [拜見着]
converb: -ing (front-vowel form; printed -žü after a back-vowel stem)

sentences.l: Küġün-Uγ̇a, Muqali, Buqa, two, sons-with-own having-audience, saying:
sentences.i: Kügün-Uqa, bringing his two sons Muqali and Buqa to an audience, said:
sentences.n: qojar 'the two' follows Muqali and Buqa, so they are the sons. köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen is köġü 'son', plural -d, -jer (the instrumental, 'with'; the bracketed (i)s are Shiratori's), and the reflexive -jen 'his own'; the Ming gives only 兒子每 自的行. aγ̇ulžažü (拜見着) is 'having an audience'. I read the father as bringing his sons before the lord.

sentences.t: "Bosoγa-jin čin-u boγ̇ol boltuγai;

morph.gloss: you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
optative, third person: let him … (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Threshold's your slave let-him-be;
sentences.i: "Let him be your slave of the threshold;
sentences.n: Bosoγa-jin čin-u boγ̇ol boltuγai: 'of the threshold, your slave, let him become'. čin-u is 'your' (či, 'you', with the stem čin-). boltuγai is the third-person optative, 'let him be'; Ming 敎做. Shiratori's quotation mark and semicolon open the oath.

sentences.t: bosoγa-dāča čin-u bulžiγ̇asu borbi in-ü hoγtol.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (back-vowel form; Shiratori's long ā) [行]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
to go round, turn aside (Ming 繞; an earlier part read it 'dodge') [繞了呵]
his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to cut (stem inferred from the Ming 割; here a bare stem, perhaps an imperative) [割]

sentences.l: Threshold-from your if-he-goes-round, heel-tendon his cut.
sentences.i: if he turns aside from your threshold, cut his heel-tendons.
sentences.n: bosoγa-dāča is 'from the threshold' (ablative, with Shiratori's long ā). bulžiγ̇asu (繞了呵) is 'if he goes round'; an earlier part read this word as 'dodge', the Ming here gives 'go round'. borbi in-ü hoγtol: 'heel-tendon his cut'. hoγtol is a bare stem, which I read as an imperative; the stem is read from the Ming 割.

sentences.t: Egüden-(n)ü čin-u emčü boγ̇ol boltuγai;

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [的]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
one's own, private (Ming 梯已, 'personal'); so 'private slave' [梯已]
optative, third person: let him … (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Door's your private slave let-him-be;
sentences.i: Let him be your private slave of the door;
sentences.n: Egüden-(n)ü is 'of the door' (genitive; the (n) is Shiratori's). emčü (梯已, 'one's own, private') qualifies boγ̇ol 'slave', so a private slave of the door. boltuγai again 'let him be'.

sentences.t: egüden-(n)eče čin-u heilüġešü eliged an-u edkežü gedkün"

morph.gloss: ablative: from (front-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [行]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
to leave, depart (stem inferred from the Ming 離) [離了呵]
their (third-person plural genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to cut out (stem inferred from the Ming 割) [割着]
to cast aside, abandon (Ming 撇) [撇]

sentences.l: Door-from your if-leaving, livers their cutting-out cast-aside
sentences.i: if they leave your door, cut out their livers and cast them aside."
sentences.n: egüden-(n)eče is 'from the door' (ablative). heilüġešü (離了呵) 'if he leaves'; eliged (肝每) 'liver(s)'; edkežü 'cutting out'; gedkün 'cast aside', a converb. an-u is the plural 'their' and goes with the plural eliged 'livers' (Ming 肝每), where the heel-tendon and life oaths have the singular in-ü; I read the penalty as falling on both sons, and heilüġešü, which has no person, as 'if they leave'. The oath's second half mirrors the first: threshold and heel-tendon, door and liver. Shiratori's quotation mark closes here.

sentences.t: keġežü ögbe.
sentences.l: saying, gave.
sentences.i: So saying, he gave them.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying', ögbe 'gave': the father gave his sons into service.

sentences.t: Čilaγ̇un-Γaiči Tüṅge, Qaši qojar köġüd(i)-jen basa Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur aγ̇ulžažü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chila'un-Gaichi, a man's name (Ming 人名; the sense of Γaiči is not known from these sources) [人名]
Tüngge, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
Qashi, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
two, the two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [自的行]
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
to have an audience, to be received, to wait on a lord (Ming 拜見) [拜見着]
converb: -ing (front-vowel form; printed -žü after a back-vowel stem)

sentences.l: Čilaγ̇un-Γaiči, Tüṅge, Qaši, the two, sons-own again Čiṅgis Qaγan-to having-audience, saying:
sentences.i: Chila'un-Gaichi, again bringing his two sons Tüngge and Qashi before Chinggis Qahan, said:
sentences.n: The same pattern as Kügün-Uqa's: qojar 'the two' follows Tüṅge and Qaši, köġüd(i)-jen is 'his own sons' (plural -d, reflexive -jen), aγ̇ulžažü 'having an audience'. basa 'again'. Qaγan-dur is the dative 'to, before' the Qahan.

sentences.t: "Altan bosoγa čin-u sakižu atuγai keġen ögbe bi.

morph.gloss: gold (noun); the Altan Qan is the Jin emperor [金]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
optative, third person: let him … (back-vowel form)
I (first-person singular pronoun; Ming 我) [我]

sentences.l: Golden threshold your guarding let-him-stay, saying gave I.
sentences.i: "Let him stay and guard your golden threshold," so saying, I gave them.
sentences.n: Altan bosoγa čin-u sakižu atuγai: 'golden threshold your guarding let-him-stay' (atuγai is the third-person optative of a- 'be, remain'). keġen 'saying', ögbe bi 'I gave' (bi is Ming 我, 'I'). The speaker is Chila'un-Gaichi, now speaking in the first person.

sentences.t: Altan bosoγa-dāča čin-u aṅgida oduγ̇asu ami in-ü tasulžu gedkün

morph.gloss: gold (noun); the Altan Qan is the Jin emperor [金]
ablative: from (back-vowel form; Shiratori's long ā) [行]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
to go (stem inferred from the Ming 去) [去呵]
his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to cut off, sever (stem inferred from the Ming 斷) [斷着]
to cast aside, abandon (Ming 撇) [撇]

sentences.l: Golden threshold-from your apart if-he-goes, life his cutting-off cast-aside;
sentences.i: If he goes elsewhere from your golden threshold, cut off his life and cast him aside;
sentences.n: aṅgida 'apart, otherwise' (Ming 別), oduγ̇asu (去呵) 'if he goes'. ami in-ü tasulžu gedkün: 'life his cutting-off cast-aside'. A parallel with the oath in the unit before.

sentences.t: örgen egüden ergüžü ögtügei keġen ögbe bi.

morph.gloss: to lift up (stem inferred from the Ming 擡) [擡着]
optative, third person: let him … (front-vowel form)
I (first-person singular pronoun; Ming 我) [我]

sentences.l: Wide door lifting let-him-give, saying gave I.
sentences.i: "Raising the wide door, let him give," so saying, I gave them.
sentences.n: örgen egüden 'wide door'; ergüžü (擡着) 'lifting up'; ögtügei 'let him give'. What he lifts and gives is not said, and the Ming 擡着 敎與 does not help; 'raising the wide door' may be a ritual figure for service. I give the words and flag the sense as uncertain.

sentences.t: Örgen egüden- (n)eče čin-u öġere oduγ̇asu öre in-ü miderižü gedkün" keġebe.

morph.gloss: door (the word is split by Shiratori's hyphen; the ending is on the next word) [門]
ablative: from (front-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [行]
you, thou (second-person singular pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你]
to go (stem inferred from the Ming 去) [去呵]
his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
to kick (stem inferred from the Ming 踢) [踢着]
to cast aside, abandon (Ming 撇) [撇]

sentences.l: Wide door-from your otherwise if-he-goes, heart his kicking cast-aside, said.
sentences.i: If he goes otherwise from the wide door, kick out his heart and cast it aside," he said.
sentences.n: Örgen egüden- (n)eče is one phrase, 'from the wide door', split by Shiratori's hyphen: the ablative (n)eče stands on its own word. öġere (別) 'otherwise', oduγ̇asu 'if he goes'. öre in-ü miderižü gedkün: 'heart his kicking, cast aside' (mideri-, stem read from the Ming 踢). keġebe 'said' closes the speech.

sentences.t: Žebke-ji Qasar-a ögbe.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel; Shiratori's -ji)
Qasar, a man's name (Chinggis's brother) [人名]

sentences.l: Žebke-(acc.) Qasar-to gave.
sentences.i: He gave Jebke to Qasar.
sentences.n: Žebke-ji is the accusative after a vowel (Shiratori writes -ji, not -i); Qasar-a is the dative (Ming 行). Who is the giver is not said.

sentences.t: Žebke Žurkin-u nutuγ-ača Boroγ̇ül neretü üčüken köġüken-i abčiražü Höġelün eke-de aγ̇ulžan ögbe.

morph.gloss: Jebke, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (spelled Žurkin here) [種(名)]
Boroqul, a boy's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
possessive: having a name, named (front-vowel form) [有的]
to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; uncertain) [將來着]
Högelün, a woman's name (personal name) [婦名]
to have an audience, to be received, to be presented (Ming 拜見) [拜見]

sentences.l: Žebke, Žurkin's camp-from Boroγ̇ül having-name little child-(acc.) bringing, Höġelün mother-to presenting gave.
sentences.i: Jebke, bringing a little boy named Boroqul from the Jurkin camp, presented him to Mother Högelün.
sentences.n: Boroγ̇ül neretü (Ming 名字有的) is 'having the name Boroγ̇ül', the possessive -tü; köġüken-i is 'little son', the accusative: the boy is the object of abčiražü 'bringing along'. Žurkin-u nutuγ-ača is 'from the Jurkin camp'. eke-de is the dative 'to mother'. aγ̇ulžan ögbe 'gave in audience, presented'. I take Jebke as the subject because he stands first; the Ming does not mark it.

sentences.t: Höġelün eke Merkid-ün nutuγ-ača oldaγsan Küčü neretü köġüken-i

morph.gloss: Högelün, a woman's name (personal name) [婦名]
to find, get (compare olba, 'got'; Ming 得了) [得了]
verbal suffix, function unclear (compare bol-da-ba; uncertain)

Küchü, a boy's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
possessive: having a name, named (front-vowel form) [有的]

sentences.l: Höġelün mother Merkid's camp-from got Küčü named little son-(acc.),
sentences.i: the little boy named Küchü, whom Mother Högelün had got from the Merkid camp,
sentences.n: oldaγsan (得了的) is ol- 'get' with an unclear -da- and the past participle -γsan, 'that was got'. The whole phrase is the long relative clause 'mother Högelün from the Merkid camp got', qualifying köġüken-i, with neretü 'having the name' before it. The four boys are listed in one run, each with the same frame, so I give each its own unit. The main verb, težiġebe, comes at the end of the section.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud-un dotora Besüd-ün nutuγ-ača oldaγsan Kököčü neretü köġüken-i

morph.gloss: to find, get (compare olba, 'got'; Ming 得了) [得了]
verbal suffix, function unclear (compare bol-da-ba; uncertain)
past participle: 'that has been …ed' (Ming 得了的) [的]
Kököchü, a boy's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
possessive: having a name, named (front-vowel form) [有的]

sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud's among Besüd's camp-from got Kököčü named little son-(acc.),
sentences.i: the little boy named Kököchü, got from the Besüd camp among the Taichi'ud,
sentences.n: The same frame. Taičiγ̇ud-un dotora is 'among the Taichi'ud' (dotora 'inside'), then Besüd-ün nutuγ-ača 'from the camp of the Besüd'. The text sets the Besüd camp inside the Taichi'ud (dotora) and says no more.

sentences.t: Tatar-un nutuγ-ača oldaγsan Šigigen-Qutuqu neretü köġüken-i

morph.gloss: to find, get (compare olba, 'got'; Ming 得了) [得了]
verbal suffix, function unclear (compare bol-da-ba; uncertain)
past participle: 'that has been …ed' (Ming 得了的) [的]

words.reading: 失吉刊-中忽禿中忽 Šigigen-Qutuqu

morph.gloss: Shigigen-Qutuqu, a boy's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
possessive: having a name, named (front-vowel form) [有的]

sentences.l: Tatar's camp-from got Šigigen-Qutuqu named little son-(acc.),
sentences.i: the little boy named Shigigen-Qutuqu, got from the Tatar camp,
sentences.n: The same frame, now Tatar-un nutuγ-ača, 'from the Tatar camp'. The name Šigigen-Qutuqu is the Ming's 人名 only.

sentences.t: Žurkin-u nutuγ-ača oldaγsan Boroγ̇ul neretü köġüken-i

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (spelled Žurkin here) [種(名)]
to find, get (compare olba, 'got'; Ming 得了) [得了]
verbal suffix, function unclear (compare bol-da-ba; uncertain)

Boroqul, a boy's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.l: Žurkin's camp-from got Boroγ̇ul named little son-(acc.):
sentences.i: and the little boy named Boroqul, got from the Jurkin camp:
sentences.n: The fourth. This is the Boroγ̇ul of §137, whom Jebke had brought; Shiratori spells him Boroγ̇ül there, Boroγ̇ul here (the Ming gives the same 人名, and the Han, 孛舌羅兀勒, is the same in both).

sentences.t: ede dörben-i ger dotora težiġerün
sentences.l: These four-(acc.) house within when-rearing,
sentences.i: when she raised these four in the house,
sentences.n: ede 'these' (plural of ene), dörben-i 'the four' (accusative, Ming 四箇行), ger dotora 'inside the house' (Ming 家裏), težiġerün 'when rearing' (time-converb -rün). The four boys of the frame above are the object.

sentences.t: Höġelün eke köġüd-teġen üdür üžekü-jin nidün süni sonosqu-jin čikin ken-e bolγaquju keġen

morph.gloss: Högelün, a woman's name (personal name) [婦名]
dative-locative + reflexive-possessive: to, for one's own (front-vowel form) [(自的)行]

sentences.l: Höġelün mother, sons-for-her-own: day seeing's eye, night hearing's ear, whom-to may-be-made? saying
sentences.i: Mother Högelün, saying, "For her own sons, the eye that sees by day, the ear that hears by night: to whom else could they be made?"
sentences.n: köġüd-teġen is 'to her own sons', the dative with the reflexive -teġen. üžekü-jin nidün is 'of the seeing, eye' and sonosqu-jin čikin 'of the hearing, ear', with the genitive -jin after a vowel: 'eye that sees by day, ear that hears by night'. ken-e bolγaquju (誰行 得做麽) is 'to whom may it be made?'; the ending -ju I read as the Ming's question particle 麽. I take it as a rhetorical question, that is, the boys are to be eyes and ears for her sons. The reading is uncertain.

sentences.t: ger dotora težiġebe.
sentences.l: House within raised.
sentences.i: and she raised them in the house.
sentences.n: ger dotora težiġebe: 'inside the house raised' (težiġe- 'bring up', past -be). Shiratori's stop closes §138.

sentences.t: Ede Žürkin irgen-ü josun Žürkin bolurun Qabul Qān-u doloγ̇an köġüd-ün aṅqa aqa Ökin-Balaqaγ büleġe.

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種(名)]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種(名)]
converb of time: when …ing (Ming 做的)
Qabul, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
qan, sovereign (the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
elder brother, the eldest (Ming 長) [長]
Ökin-Barqaq, a man's name (Ming 人名; Shiratori prints Balaqaγ here, Barqaγ in §§48–49) [人名]

sentences.l: These Žürkin people's reason: Žürkin when-becoming, Qabul Qān's seven sons' first elder Ökin-Balaqaγ was.
sentences.i: The account of these Jurkin people: when the Jurkin came to be, the eldest of Qabul Qahan's seven sons was Ökin-Barqaq.
sentences.n: josun is 'custom, way, reason', Ming 理: 'the reason of these Jurkin people', and the account that follows is the reason for the name. Žürkin bolurun is 'when Jurkin was becoming' (bol-, time-converb -urun). Then genitives before their nouns: Qabul Qān-u doloγ̇an köġüd-ün aṅqa aqa, 'Qabul Qan's seven sons' eldest' (aṅqa Ming 最, aqa Ming 長, 'most, eldest'). Shiratori prints Ökin-Balaqaγ here (Han 巴剌…, a different transcription), where §§48–49 print Ökin-Barqaγ (巴舌兒…). He is the eldest of Qabul's seven sons in both places, so I take them to be the same man and in the English use the earlier form.

sentences.t: Köġün in-ü Sorqatu-Žürki büleġe.

morph.gloss: his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]

words.reading: 莎舌兒中合禿-主舌兒乞 Sorqatu-Žürki

glyphs.s: 莎舌兒中合禿-主舌兒乞

morph.gloss: Sorqatu-Jurki, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]

sentences.l: Son his Sorqatu-Žürki was.
sentences.i: His son was Sorqatu-Jurki.
sentences.n: Köġün in-ü: 'son his', the possessor after the noun. Sorqatu-Žürki is the Ming's 人名. büleġe 'was'. The earlier mention of Ökin-Barqaq's son (§49) names him Qutuγtu-Jürki; this section prints Sorqatu-Žürki, as §122 does, and the text does not say whether they are one man.

sentences.t: Žürkin bolurun Qabul Qān-u köġüd-ün aqa keġežü irgen-ü-ġen dotorāča ilγažu

morph.gloss: the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種(名)]
converb of time: when …ing (Ming 做的)
Qabul, a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
qan, sovereign (the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
elder brother, the eldest (Ming 長) [長]
genitive: of … (it stands before dotor 'inside'; the reflexive -ġen follows; as Shiratori divides it; a linking vowel is also possible)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (Ming 自的行) [自的行]
ablative: from (back-vowel form; the long vowel runs the stem vowel into the ending) [行]
to pick out, separate (Ming 揀) [揀着]

sentences.l: Žürkin when-becoming, Qabul Qān's sons' eldest saying, people-own from-among picking-out,
sentences.i: When the Jurkin came to be, the eldest of Qabul Qahan's sons, so saying, picked out from among his own people
sentences.n: The same opening, then keġežü 'saying', irgen-ü-ġen dotorāča 'from inside his own people' (ablative -āča; the genitive -ü and reflexive -ġen before it) and ilγažu 'picking out' (Ming 揀着). The Ming 說着 after 長 reads oddly; I take it as 'so saying', then the picking. The sentence is long and runs on for five units, to teimü in unit 51.

sentences.t: helige-dür šülšütü heregei-dür hončitan aγ̇ušigi duγ̇uraṅ žirügetü

morph.gloss: gallbladder, courage (Ming 膽; stem uncertain) [膽]
thumb (Ming 大拇指; stem uncertain) [大拇指]
able to shoot arrows (Ming 能發箭的; analysis uncertain) [能發箭的]

sentences.l: Liver-in gall-having, thumb-in arrow-shooting-able, lung full, heart-having,
sentences.i: men with gall in the liver, able to shoot with the thumb, with full lungs, with a heart,
sentences.n: A string of body-part idioms for courage and strength, each read from the Ming: helige-dür šülšütü (肝行 膽有的) 'in the liver, having gall'; heregei-dür hončitan (大拇指行 能發箭的) 'in the thumb, able to shoot'; aγ̇ušigi duγ̇uraṅ (肺 滿) 'lung full'; žirügetü (心有的) 'having a heart'. The possessive -tü, -tan 'having'. The stems are partly uncertain. These are all objects of ilγažu below, one long noun phrase broken for reading.

sentences.t: aman düġüreṅ aγ̇urtan ere tutum erdemüdten bökös küčüten-i

morph.gloss: spirit, fierce energy (Ming 剛氣; stem uncertain) [剛氣]
each, every one (Ming 各各) [各各]

sentences.l: Mouth full, spirited men, each skilled, sturdy ones, strong ones-(acc.),
sentences.i: mouths full, spirited men, each of them skilled, sturdy, strong,
sentences.n: aman düġüreṅ 'mouth full'; aγ̇urtan ere 'men having spirit' (Ming 剛氣 丈夫); tutum erdemüdten 'each having skill' (Ming 各各 技能有的每); bökös 'sturdy ones' (bökö 'strong' with plural -s), küčüten-i 'those having strength', in the accusative. The accusative -i belongs to the whole noun phrase.

sentences.t: ilγažu ögčü aγ̇urtan šülšüten omoγtan žürkimes

morph.gloss: to pick out, separate (Ming 揀) [揀着]
spirit, fierce energy (Ming 氣; stem uncertain) [氣]
gallbladder, courage (Ming 膽; stem uncertain) [膽]
daring, courage (Ming 勇; stem uncertain) [勇]
(those) whom none can withstand (Ming 無人能敵每); the word that explains the name Žürkin; analysis uncertain [(無人能敵每)]

sentences.l: picking-out giving, spirited, gall-having, daring-having, those-none-can-withstand
sentences.i: picking them out and giving them: the spirited, the stout-hearted, the bold, those no one could withstand
sentences.n: ilγažu ögčü 'picking out, giving' (Ming 揀着 與着). What is given, and to whom, the Ming does not say. aγ̇urtan šülšüten omoγtan are three more 'those having' words (spirit, gall, daring); žürkimes (無人能敵每) is 'those no one can withstand', the word the next unit ties to the clan name.

sentences.t: tula Žürkin keġegdekü josun teimü.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of') [上頭]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種(名)]
so, thus, it is so [那般有]

sentences.l: because Žürkin being-called reason thus.
sentences.i: That is why they are called Jurkin: such is the reason.
sentences.n: tula (上頭) is 'because of'; Žürkin keġegdekü is 'called Jurkin' (keġe- 'say' with the passive -gde- and the participle -kü), josun teimü 'the reason is so'. The text derives the name from žürkimes, 'those none can withstand'; the sound is near and the Ming's 無人能敵 supports it, but the derivation is the chronicler's, not mine. Shiratori's stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Teimün omoγtan irgen-i Čiṅgis Qaγan doraitaγ̇ulžu Žürkin oboγtu-ji ülidkebe.

morph.gloss: such, of that kind (Ming 那般; related to tein 'thus') [那般]
daring, courage (Ming 勇; stem uncertain) [勇]
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]

words.reading: 朶舌剌亦塔兀(勒)周 doraitaγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: to submit, be subdued (stem uncertain; Ming 服下) [服下了着]
the Jurkin, a Mongol clan (clan name) [種(名)]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel; Shiratori's -ji) [行]
to destroy, wipe out (Ming 敎毀滅了; stem uncertain) [敎毀滅了]

sentences.l: Such bold people-(acc.) Čiṅgis Qaγan subduing, Žürkin clan-having-(acc.) destroyed.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan subdued those bold people, and wiped out the clan-holding Jurkin.
sentences.n: Teimün omoγtan irgen-i: 'such, those having daring, people' (accusative). doraitaγ̇ulžu (服下了着) 'having made submit' (causative -γ̇ul-). oboγtu-ji is 'those having a clan-name' (oboγ 'clan', Ming 姓有的); I read it as the Jurkin proper, the clan lineage. ülidkebe (敎毀滅了) 'destroyed'; the stem is uncertain. Shiratori's stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Irgen-i ulus-i in-ü Čiṅgis Qaγan öġer-ün emčü irgen bolγaba.

morph.gloss: people, realm, households (Ming 人烟) [人烟]
his, her, their (third-person genitive stem; it stands after its noun) [他]
Chinggis, a man's name (the title taken by Temüjin in 1206) [太祖︀]
own, self (Ming 自的; as in the earlier öġer-ün, 自己(的)) [自]
one's own, private (Ming 梯已, 'personal') [梯已]
people, subjects (the common folk of a camp or realm) [百姓]

sentences.l: People-(acc.) realm-(acc.) his, Čiṅgis Qaγan own's private people made-to-become.
sentences.i: Their people and households Chinggis Qahan made his own private people.
sentences.n: Irgen-i ulus-i: 'people, realm', both accusative (Ming 百姓 人烟). in-ü is 'their' here, after its nouns. öġer-ün (自的) is 'own' here, as in the earlier parts: öġer-ün emčü irgen, 'own private people'. bolγaba is bol- 'become' with the causative -γa- and the past: 'caused to become'.
